name: Mirissa
description: A crescent-shaped beach famous for whale watching and a laid-back vibe. One of Sri Lanka's most photogenic coastal spots with turquoise waters and swaying palms.
attractions: Whale watching tours, Parrot Rock, Secret Beach, Mirissa Beach, Coconut Tree Hill
travel_tips: Book whale watching at dawn for best sightings. Avoid blue whale season rush by going mid-week. Many guesthouses offer great sea views.
highlights: Blue whale sightings, stunning sunsets, fresh seafood

name: Unawatuna
description: A sheltered bay near Galle with calm waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling. Surrounded by coral reefs and a vibrant cafe culture.
attractions: Jungle Beach, Rumassala Hill, Japanese Peace Pagoda, Snorkeling spots
travel_tips: Great base for day trips to Galle Fort. The bay is naturally protected so waters are calm year-round.
highlights: Calm snorkeling bay, Galle day trips, lively nightlife

name: Arugam Bay
description: A legendary surf destination on the east coast with consistent waves and a bohemian atmosphere. Famous among surfers worldwide.
attractions: Main Point surf break, Pottuvil Point, Crocodile Rock, Whisky Point
travel_tips: East coast season is opposite to west so great for May-September. Rent a scooter to explore nearby lagoons.
highlights: World-class surfing, leopard safaris nearby, stunning lagoons

name: Tangalle
description: A serene and unspoiled stretch of southern coastline known for its wide beaches and turtle nesting sites. Less touristy and more tranquil.
attractions: Rekawa Beach turtle nesting, Hummanaya Blowhole, Mulkirigala Rock Temple
travel_tips: Watch sea turtles nesting at Rekawa Beach at night with a ranger. Very peaceful and uncrowded.
highlights: Sea turtle nesting, blowholes, peaceful atmosphere

name: Nilaveli
description: A pristine white sand beach in the north with crystal clear water and access to Pigeon Island Marine Park. Remote and stunningly beautiful.
attractions: Pigeon Island Marine Park, snorkeling, Trincomalee temples
travel_tips: Combine with Trincomalee hot springs and temples. Pigeon Island has some of Sri Lanka's best snorkeling.
highlights: Pigeon Island snorkeling, untouched white sands, remote feel

name: Bentota
description: A popular beach resort town combining lagoon water sports with golden beaches. Great for watersports and Ayurveda retreats.
attractions: Bentota Lagoon, watersports, Brief Garden, Kosgoda Turtle Hatchery
travel_tips: Take a boat safari on the Bentota lagoon. Visit the turtle hatchery at Kosgoda just 10km away.
highlights: Water sports, lagoon safaris, Ayurveda spas

name: Hikkaduwa
description: A classic beach town with a long coral reef and a lively atmosphere. Popular for surfing and glass-bottom boat rides.
attractions: Hikkaduwa Coral Reef, Sea Turtle spotting, Blow Hole, Hikkaduwa Lake
travel_tips: Rent a bicycle to explore the coast. The coral reef is walkable at low tide in some sections.
highlights: Coral reef snorkeling, surfing, vibrant nightlife

name: Pasikuda
description: A uniquely shallow lagoon-style beach that extends almost a kilometer with knee-deep calm water. Ideal for families.
attractions: Shallow lagoon beach, Kalkudah beach, watersports
travel_tips: The shallow water makes it perfect for families with children. Book well ahead as it is a popular spot.
highlights: Shallow calm waters, family-friendly, pristine sands

name: Kandy
description: The cultural capital of Sri Lanka and home to the sacred Temple of the Tooth Relic. Set around a beautiful lake surrounded by forested hills.
attractions: Temple of the Tooth, Kandy Lake, Royal Botanical Gardens Peradeniya, Kandyan Cultural Show, Udawatte Kele Sanctuary
travel_tips: Don't miss the evening Kandyan dance performance. Visit the Peradeniya Botanical Gardens early morning.
highlights: Sacred Temple of the Tooth, Kandyan dance, lush botanical gardens

name: Anuradhapura
description: The ancient first capital of Sri Lanka with ruins spanning over 2000 years. A UNESCO World Heritage Site with sacred Buddhist monuments.
attractions: Sacred Bo Tree, Ruwanwelisaya Dagoba, Jetavanarama Stupa, Abhayagiri Monastery, Isurumuniya Temple
travel_tips: Rent a bicycle to cover the vast archaeological site. Dress modestly as this is an active religious site.
highlights: Ancient dagobas, sacred Bo tree over 2200 years old, UNESCO site

name: Polonnaruwa
description: Sri Lanka's second ancient capital with remarkably preserved ruins including the famous Gal Vihara rock sculptures.
attractions: Gal Vihara rock sculptures, Parakrama Samudra lake, Rankoth Vehera, Lankatilaka Image House
travel_tips: Combine with a Minneriya safari day trip. Hire a local guide to understand the historical context.
highlights: Magnificent rock sculptures, medieval architecture, ancient reservoirs

name: Sigiriya
description: The iconic Lion Rock fortress rising 200m above the jungle. A UNESCO World Heritage Site with ancient frescoes and panoramic views.
attractions: Sigiriya Rock Fortress, Frescoes Gallery, Mirror Wall, Water Gardens, Pidurangala Rock
travel_tips: Climb Pidurangala Rock at sunrise for the best view of Sigiriya without the crowds.
highlights: Iconic rock fortress, ancient frescoes, breathtaking summit views

name: Dambulla
description: Home to the most impressive cave temple complex in Sri Lanka with five caves filled with over 150 Buddha statues and ancient paintings.
attractions: Dambulla Cave Temple UNESCO, Golden Temple, Dambulla Market
travel_tips: Combine with a Sigiriya day trip as they are only 20km apart. Visit the cave temple in the morning.
highlights: Ancient cave paintings, 150 plus Buddha statues, UNESCO World Heritage

name: Ella
description: A charming hill station surrounded by tea plantations waterfalls and breathtaking mountain views. Famous for the Nine Arch Bridge and hiking trails.
attractions: Nine Arch Bridge, Little Adam's Peak, Ella Rock, Ravana Falls, Rawana Ella Cave
travel_tips: Take the famous train from Kandy or Nuwara Eliya. Hike Little Adam's Peak at sunrise.
highlights: Iconic Nine Arch Bridge, tea country hikes, scenic train rides

name: Nuwara Eliya
description: Known as Little England for its cool climate and colonial architecture. Surrounded by tea estates and is the heart of Sri Lanka's tea country.
attractions: Victoria Park, Gregory Lake, Tea factory tours, Horton Plains, Hakgala Botanical Garden
travel_tips: Visit a working tea factory for a tour and tasting. The town gets foggy and cold at night so bring a jacket.
highlights: Tea estate tours, colonial charm, cool mountain climate

name: Sinharaja
description: Sri Lanka's only remaining tropical rainforest and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. A biodiversity hotspot with endemic birds and rare wildlife.
attractions: Rainforest trekking, Bird watching, Endemic species, Guided nature walks
travel_tips: Always go with a registered guide. Leeches are present so wear appropriate footwear.
highlights: Endemic bird species, virgin rainforest, exceptional biodiversity

name: Horton Plains
description: A misty plateau at 2100m altitude with unique cloud forest ecosystems. Famous for World's End cliff with dramatic drops into the lowland forest.
attractions: World's End viewpoint, Baker's Falls, Cloud forest trails
travel_tips: Start the trek before 7am to catch the view before clouds roll in. The plateau is cold so bring warm layers.
highlights: World's End cliff drop, misty cloud forest, endemic wildlife

name: Knuckles
description: A rugged mountain range with dramatic peaks deep valleys and rural village life. UNESCO-listed with exceptional biodiversity and trekking routes.
attractions: Trekking trails, Corbett's Gap, Village homestays, Bird watching
travel_tips: Multi-day treks are available with village homestays. One of Sri Lanka's most underrated hiking destinations.
highlights: Remote mountain trekking, rural village culture, misty peaks

name: Yala
description: Sri Lanka's most famous national park with the world's highest density of leopards. Also home to elephants sloth bears crocodiles and 200 bird species.
attractions: Leopard safaris, Elephant herds, Sloth bear sightings, Block 1 game drives
travel_tips: Book Block 1 for best leopard sightings. Go on multiple game drives for better chances.
highlights: Highest leopard density in world, diverse big game, coastal park scenery

name: Udawalawe
description: A premier elephant sanctuary offering near-guaranteed elephant sightings. Famous for large elephant herds coming to the reservoir at dusk.
attractions: Elephant herds, Elephant Transit Home, Reservoir views, Bird watching
travel_tips: Visit the Elephant Transit Home where orphaned baby elephants are fed at 9am 12pm 3pm and 6pm.
highlights: Guaranteed elephant herds, Elephant Transit Home, peaceful reservoir

name: Wilpattu
description: Sri Lanka's largest national park with a unique landscape of natural lakes called villus. Less visited than Yala but offers superb leopard sightings.
attractions: Leopard spotting, Sloth bears, Deer, Crocodile, Natural villa lakes
travel_tips: Much less crowded than Yala with equally good leopard chances. The villa lake landscape is unique.
highlights: Pristine natural lakes, excellent leopard sightings, fewer crowds

name: Minneriya
description: Famous for The Gathering the largest elephant congregation in Asia where hundreds of elephants meet at the reservoir.
attractions: The Gathering elephant event, Reservoir game drives, Bird watching
travel_tips: Plan visit between August and October for the famous Gathering. Combine with Sigiriya and Polonnaruwa.
highlights: World's largest elephant gathering, up to 300 elephants, scenic reservoir

name: Colombo
description: A vibrant modern capital blending Dutch colonial history with contemporary skyscrapers. Exciting food scene and coastal promenade walks.
attractions: Galle Face Green, Pettah Market, National Museum, Gangaramaya Temple, Colombo Fort, Viharamahadevi Park, Beira Lake
travel_tips: Try street food at Galle Face Green in the evening. Take a tuk-tuk for short trips. The Pettah Market is fascinating.
highlights: Diverse food scene, colonial architecture, modern city life

name: Galle
description: A magnificent Dutch colonial fort town on the southern tip of Sri Lanka. UNESCO-listed with cobblestone streets boutique hotels and ocean views from the ramparts.
attractions: Galle Fort, Dutch Reformed Church, National Maritime Museum, Ramparts walk, Boutique shopping
travel_tips: Walk the ramparts at sunset. The fort has excellent cafes and boutique shops. Stay inside the fort for the full experience.
highlights: UNESCO colonial fort, boutique dining, Indian Ocean rampart walks

name: Adams Peak
description: A sacred pilgrimage mountain known as Sri Pada with a famous footprint at its summit. Climbed by pilgrims of all faiths especially at full moon.
attractions: Summit pilgrimage, Sri Pada footprint, Sunrise views, Waterfall trail
travel_tips: The climb starts at 2am to catch sunrise from the summit. The path is lit with lights during pilgrimage season.
highlights: Sacred mountain pilgrimage, spectacular sunrise, multi-faith significance
